input.quote: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: The audit right is written, uses an independent accountant chosen by mutual agreement, is limited to accounting records (no system access) and Licensor bears cost unless a 5% discrepancy is found — all at or better than our position — but there is no cap on how often audits may be requested, so the fallback "once per year" limit fails. Our edit adds only the annual frequency and business-hours limits.

input.quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge is payable by Licensee; fees are usage-based and Article XXIII expressly excludes termination damages. We note Licensor retains fees for trades already executed on termination, which is ordinary accrued consideration rather than an LD.

input.quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
input.rationale: The Agreement is pure "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed, including any warranty that the platform meets its documentation or operates securely — exactly our walk-away position. We inserted the fallback warranty set (workmanlike performance, 90-day conformance to Documentation, no malicious code) with repair/replace/refund, carved out of the disclaimer.

input.quote: (i) FORCE MAJEURE. Except for the obligations to make payments hereunder, each Party shall be relieved of the obligations hereunder
input.rationale: There is no insurance covenant anywhere; the only reference to insurance is as a cost we pay under the payment clause. For a vendor hosting the trading platform and our trade data this is a gap, so we inserted a short insurance paragraph (GL, E&O, cyber) in the general provisions; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback.
